question.text: The IPEV Valuation Guidelines (Dec 2022) summarise the 'most widely used' valuation methods for portfolio companies. Which of the following is NOT among the seven methods listed?

answer.text: Price of previous transaction (for follow-on investments)
Net asset valuation (NAV) for loss-making or financial businesses
Industry metrics (GMV, ARPU, value per subscriber)

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per PDF Section 11.8.3, the seven IPEV methods are: (1) Price of previous transaction, (2) Early-stage companies (milestone/scenario/OPM), (3) Multiples Approach, (4) NAV, (5) DCF, (6) Valuation of Debt Investments, (7) Industry Metrics. Black-Scholes for ESOPs is an accounting-for-employee-grants method (Ind-AS 102), NOT a portfolio investee valuation method. **The Trap:** All three correct methods appear verbatim in the IPEV list. Black-Scholes for ESOPs is tempting because options and OPM are mentioned (OPM is listed under the early-stage method (#2)) — but OPM (Option Pricing Method for equity allocation) is different from ESOP grant-date fair value. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests the 7 IPEV methods. Ind-AS 102 (Share-based Payment) ESOP valuation is tested in CA Final and CFA L2. Do not conflate the two. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** In your valuer engagement letter, specify WHICH of the 7 IPEV methods will be used for each asset class in your portfolio. This pre-commitment reduces disputes later and aligns the valuer's approach with your PPM disclosures.
